question: The Stagnone Islands Nature Reserve, which includes SPA ITA010028 and SAC ITA010001, is increasingly affected by unsustainable anthropic pressure. The protected area is subject to construction abuses, vineyards are being uprooted there, the number of prefabricated buildings is mushrooming, and unauthorised parking, waste dumping, fires, illegal fishing and vehicular traffic are commonplace there.

The managing body Libero Consorzio Comunale di Trapani (Free Municipal Consortium of Trapani) gives the green light – by way of derogation – to almost all the activities prohibited by the natural reserve regulations issued by the Sicilian Region (Executive Order 198 of 24 May 2000).

The site is used by thousands of kitesurfers, an activity that has very serious consequences for the natural environment and is in breach of Directive 92/43/EEC, since the events organised, financed by the Sicilian Region and Marsala municipality, are allegedly carried out without any environmental impact assessment.

Lastly, the reserve lacks a scientific committee, nature trails, surveillance and measures to protect the lagoon’s biodiversity. It does not even have any signs indicating that it is a nature reserve. In view of this: 1.
Can the Commission provide information on the actual implementation of the Habitats and Birds Directives in the above-mentioned Natura 2000 sites?
What view does it take of the failure to carry out an environmental impact assessment for all the above activities in those areas?
answer: The Commission has no specific information on the activities mentioned by the Honourable Member on Marsala’s Stagnone Islands Nature Reserve and on the alleged environmental degradation referred to.

As the above-mentioned reserve is part of the Natura 2000 network, according to Article 6 of the Habitats Directive (1), Member States shall establish the necessary conservation measures for the site and shall take the appropriate steps to avoid the deterioration of natural habitats and the habitats of species as well as the disturbance of the species for which the site has been designated.

Furthermore, any plan or project that is likely to have a significant impact on a Natura 2000 site, either individually or in combination with other plans or projects, must be subject to an assessment of its impacts in view of the site's conservation objectives. The Commission has produced several guidance documents to help Member States’ authorities implement the above-mentioned provisions (2).

Italy has transposed these provisions in its national legislation (3) and has adopted tailored national guidelines to facilitate and ensure their consistent implementation across its regions (4). As regards the assessment of plans and projects, the Sicilian region has adopted relevant and updated guidelines as well (5).
Without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of the Treaties, Member States are primarily responsible to ensure compliance with EU environmental law.

Directive 92/43/EEC on the conservation of natural habitats and of wild fauna and flora, OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7-50. https://ec.europa.eu/environment/nature/natura2000/management/guidance_en.htm https://www.mase.gov.it/pagina/direttiva-habitat, https://www.mase.gov.it/pagina/direttiva-uccelli https://www.mase.gov.it/pagina/documenti-di-riferimento-lindividuazione-di-obiettivi-e-misure-di-conservazione, https://www.

Therefore, it is for the competent Italian authorities to ensure that the above-mentioned provisions are effectively implemented and enforced and that the designated sites are properly protected, managed and, where necessary, restored.
